claims.text: A persistent protective oxide forms above 900 °C only when the CrFeCoNiX alloy is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
Single-phase homogeneity ensures an even, surface-accessible supply of Al and Cr.
A multiphase or segregated microstructure partitions Al and Cr unevenly.
Microstructural segregation disrupts selective oxidation and produces heterogeneous, unstable oxide scales.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi are especially predisposed to segregation.
In a homogeneous Al-containing alloy, Al and Cr selectively oxidize to produce α-Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
The resulting α-Al2O3 and Cr2O3 scales are thin, slow-growing, and adherent.
CrMnFeCoNi can form Mn-dominated non-protective oxides and mixed Mn-Fe-Cr oxides during high-temperature oxidation.
Si-based oxides act as unstable competing oxide species in CrFeCoNiSi.
Different oxide growth rates and thermal-expansion mismatches generate stresses that crack or spall the scale.
Single-phase homogeneous alloys exhibit coherent, adherent scales with parabolic oxidation kinetics.
Multiphase or segregated alloys develop thicker and more heterogeneous oxide scales.
Multiphase or segregated alloys oxidize faster initially than homogeneous single-phase alloys.
Multiphase or segregated alloys provide poorer long-term protection and are more prone to cracking or spallation.
Choosing Al as X favors protective oxide formation relative to choosing Mn or Si.
Exposure above 900 °C for at least about five hours is sufficient for the hypothesized scale evolution to be assessed.

contradictions.description: The protective condition requires balanced availability of both Al and Cr, but the stated CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi compositions contain no Al. The mechanism therefore cannot apply as written to all three allowed choices of X.

The conditions define a same-nominal-composition comparison differing only in microstructure, whereas the baseline also proposes comparing X = Al against X = Mn or Si. The latter changes composition and microstructure tendency simultaneously and is not the stated controlled baseline.
